absent: How hierarchy allocation and release and activation and deactivation and translation and debug display behave beyond table linkage is not shown.
How generic allocation obtains hardware numbers and handles affinity hints and instance cookies and how preparation of interrupts interacts with hardware tables is not shown.
How release paths dismantle descriptors and how domain removal interacts with firmware linkage lifetime and power linkage is not shown.
How bus identity values and hardware maximums and per device limits and firmware matching and naming uniqueness are defined is not shown.
How affinity selection and pending movement and effective linkage computation and node assignment and default propagation are implemented is not shown.
How suspension and restoration are scheduled and how external synchronization and scoped bus acquisition behave and how chip capability flags are defined is not shown.
How individual interrupt proc entries are created and removed and how user input parsing handles malformed data beyond error propagation is not shown.
How handler installation and handler data and chip private data are consumed after initialization and how architecture isolation testing is decided is not shown.

findings.text: Three public constructors are available for message interrupt hierarchies covering a generic child domain creation path plus a parent domain instantiation path plus a per device domain installation path that binds duplicated configuration and firmware linkage into the requesting device slot.

A family of public helpers supports allocating and releasing message interrupts over ranges and full hardware extents and single positions together with matching a device domain by bus identity plus retrieving domain private information plus testing isolation across ancestry plus delegating parent initialization.

System power transition entry points provide suspension of all eligible descriptors plus late restoration of all eligible descriptors plus early restoration through a registered system core hook plus targeted rearming of a single wakeup descriptor.

Proc based inspection and control entry points expose per interrupt affinity and list forms and effective forms and hint and node identity and spurious counters plus global default affinity plus directory initialization plus a weak architecture extension for additional display.

Child hierarchy creation rejects hardware capacities above the implementation maximum while treating zero as a request for the maximum then completes missing operation hooks and chip hooks according to flags then links into the parent with message marking and records firmware linkage and bus identity and device association with optional power device inheritance.

When no operation collection is supplied the built in collection is adopted and when flagged for default assistance any absent individual hook is supplied from built in defaults while preserving supplied hooks with preparation clearing caller storage and reporting success and teardown having no effect and descriptor linkage recording the descriptor and number retrieval returning the stored number and initialization binding chip linkage and optionally installing handler linkage when handler identity is present.
Chip assistance requires both suppression and release capabilities and otherwise aborts execution while affinity assistance is installed only when absent and affinity suppression is not requested.

Parent instantiation normalizes extent to at least the hardware maximum and marks message parent status and selects bus identity from parent operations with instantiation failure reported as absence while success stores parent operations for later delegation.

Per device installation succeeds only with a message parent plus an identifier inside the per device limit plus duplicable configuration plus usable firmware linkage plus existing descriptor storage plus an empty slot plus successful parent initialization plus successful hierarchy linkage plus successful preparation with any failure leaving the slot empty and transient resources released and success transferring ownership of duplicated configuration and allocated linkage.

Device matching holds only for message device domains whose bus identity equals the query while isolation is indicated when any ancestor carries the isolated marking or when the architecture test indicates isolation and information retrieval exposes host private storage as message information.

Allocation requires valid control and an existing domain and optionally ensures simple descriptors when flagged before preferring a custom allocator when present and otherwise using the generic path with failure followed by release. Range helpers derive counts from inclusive boundaries while full extent helpers span from zero through hardware extent minus one.

Suspension skips descriptors lacking actions and chained descriptors and those with deferred depth with wakeup enabled descriptors becoming armed and possibly temporarily enabled for chip wakeup while remaining descriptors become marked and disabled with additional chip level suppression when the chip requests it and arming or marking signals a need for external synchronization.

Restoration clears armed marking and reverses suspend time enabling before reenabling marked descriptors while leaving unmarked descriptors untouched unless forced depth requires synthesizing disabled and suppressed state prior to enabling. Targeted rearming applies solely to marked wakeup descriptors and clears marking while arming and enabling.

Affinity display prefers pending linkage when a move is pending and otherwise configured linkage while effective display uses effective linkage where supported with list and bitmap textual forms distinguished. Updates require user permission and global enablement and allocated working storage with masks lacking any online processor refused and empty selections delegated to architecture choice and other selections applied through the affinity setter. Global default updates similarly require overlap with online processors.

A per device descriptor guard serializes device domain installation and slot occupancy checks plus device domain matching lookups plus public range and full extent and single position allocation and release paths with locked suffix variants assuming the caller already holds the guard.

A per descriptor raw spinlock with interrupt exclusion protects suspension evaluation and restoration handling plus affinity and hint inspection with suspension acquiring per descriptor before possible external synchronization and restoration holding across handling and hint copying occurring under scope before formatting outside the critical section.

The hierarchy table provides roles for translation and activation and release and allocation and deactivation with optional debug display. The default message set provides roles for number retrieval and initialization and preparation and teardown and descriptor linkage.

Parent linkage records parent operations and message parent marking and normalized extent and bus selection while child linkage records host information and device association and bus identity with optional power inheritance and per device bundles record hardware extent and chip and operations and private data and allocation storage and generated naming. Proc linkage records a global directory pointer plus per file operation roles for open and sequential read and seek and release with write present on mutable controls plus a constraint record holding header control and numeric precision and chip width.

Descriptors move among active and marked and armed and temporarily enabled conditions with suspension creating marked or armed outcomes and restoration returning toward active while forced depth creates a synthesized disabled path and early versus late restoration phases separate urgent wakeup handling from general restoration with system core revival triggering the early phase.

Device domains move from absent to installed only after all preconditions and preparation succeed with failure returning to absent and allocated interrupts move from validated control through descriptor assurance to allocated with failure rolling back to released.

Missing suppression or release capability aborts during chip assistance while missing parent linkage or initialization hook triggers a one time warning and failure and attempting to reuse an occupied device slot triggers a one time warning and failure leaving prior state intact.

Invalid control or absent domain fails allocation with distinct error indications and allocation failure invokes release before reporting. Affinity writes fail when permission or global enablement or working storage is unavailable and selections without online overlap are refused to preserve usability with empty selections handled through architecture fallback.

Arming for wakeup requires external synchronization to ensure visibility before suspension completes and suspend time enabling must later be reversed to restore original disabled state while forced restoration must synthesize disabled state to keep depth accounting consistent.
Two virtual interrupt state indicators are defined with the reservation eligibility indicator valued at one and the activation indicator valued at two.

Proc display constraints default to a numeric precision of four and a chip width of eight with header printing initially disabled. Two alternative name length limits exist valued at one hundred twenty eight and eleven. The architecture descriptor marker uses a fixed address sentinel valued at four thousand three hundred sixty nine. The actual interrupt count aliases the total count.

The interrupt directory name is irq and the default smp affinity control lives under that directory with owner writable and world readable permissions. Spurious reporting presents total count plus unhandled count plus recent unhandled timing in milliseconds. Affinity reporting distinguishes four selectors ordered from zero through three covering standard and list and effective and effective list views.
